# iBluSend

Connect one iBluSend workspace to inspect conversations, contacts, devices, groups, delivery status, opt-out state, and bot status. Draft and send only after showing the exact destination and content for approval. If the person ticks them when connecting, it can also read reports, templates, campaigns and the calendar, save template and campaign drafts, and prepare booking links they confirm in the app.

## Connection

This plugin connects to `https://api.iblusend.com/functions/v1/agent-api/v1/mcp/public` using the host's remote HTTP MCP support.
OAuth discovery is server-driven. Do not add an API key, access token, client secret, or static
Authorization header to this package.

## Included workflows

- `inbox-triage`: read-only review and action list.
- `safe-draft-and-send`: exact preview, explicit confirmation, one send, status check.
- `contact-device-compliance`: inspect one contact/device or confirm one opt-out/bot change.
- `reports`: read the Reports page numbers.
- `templates`: read message templates and save a template the person approves.
- `campaigns`: read campaigns and save a draft the person launches in the app.
- `calendar`: read appointments and open times, and prepare booking links the person confirms.

## Messaging tools

The connection is bound to one workspace per consent grant. Every OAuth grant discovers the same
thirteen messaging tools. A Read-only grant can use the ten read tools; the three action tools return
an `insufficient_scope` challenge before validation or dispatch. Read and act authorizes those
actions, which still require host confirmation. Public OAuth sends are 1:1 only; group conversations
remain readable. This plugin is not a bulk sender.

## Optional areas

On the Connect screen the person can also tick optional areas. Nothing is ticked for them. Each
area is its own OAuth scope; a draft scope comes only with Read and act.

| Area | Read scope | Draft scope | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reports | `reports:read` | none | `get_report` |
| Templates | `templates:read` | `templates:drafts:write` | `list_templates`, `get_template`, `create_template`, `update_template` |
| Campaigns | `campaigns:read` | `campaigns:drafts:write` | `list_campaigns`, `get_campaign`, `list_campaign_audiences`, `create_campaign_draft`, `update_campaign_draft` |
| Calendar | `calendar:read` | none | `list_appointments`, `get_appointment`, `get_availability`, `list_meeting_types`, `draft_booking`, `draft_appointment_change` |

Every grant discovers these sixteen area tools. A call without its area returns
`insufficient_scope`; the person reconnects and ticks that area. Connections made earlier keep
what they granted. Nothing in an area sends, launches or books: a campaign launches only when the
person presses Launch in the app, and a booking or change happens only when they press Schedule or
Save. Workflows, bots and voice agents are further optional areas; their tools also need the
workspace owner and that feature turned on.
